build_commit: f561c0e5 (experimental tip, deployed to the Deck with deck_deploy at about 18:18 EDT by runbook A)
screen: MONITOR (855 x 766 per runbook A); screenshot after the chord taken at 1920 x 1080 composited.

setup.board: 'Espressif Systems ESP32S3_DEV' (vendor 303a, product 1001), handlers: event9 and js1. Two 'Microsoft X-Box 360 pad' virtual pads sit beside it (event6/js0 and event23/js2). Files: /dev/input/event9 is root:input, mode rw-rw----, with an ACL entry giving user deck rw (so the reader opened it); js1 is rw-rw-r--. The deck user is in groups deck, steamos-log-submitter, wheel (not input). So the event node was readable; the js node was not needed.
setup.reader: p89_evread.py copied to /tmp on the Deck. The runbook's start line (setsid nohup timeout 12 python3 ... &) left an empty file and no process twice, in a plain ssh. I used 'systemd-run --user --collect' with the output going to the file instead (journal showed the reader running). Then it worked. Run on /dev/input/event9 for 10 s.
setup.start_state: Quick Access closed (closed with the chord beforehand), Home page showing, no game. Steam main menu read by the MainMenu page's visibilityState: 'hidden' (2 x 1 px window) before every press.
setup.menu_detection_note: I judge 'menu opened' by the MainMenu_uid2 page's visibilityState turning visible and its size growing. It stayed hidden at 2 x 1 every time. I did not take a screenshot after the Steam-button presses, so the by-eye check is missing; the chord's own Quick Access opening was confirmed by the QuickAccess page turning visible and a screenshot.

pressed: deck_pressButton GUIDE held 80 ms, 150 ms, 400 ms (one try each, counted), then deck_pressChord GUIDE+A. A stray earlier press: one GUIDE 80 ms press (no reader running) while I found out the reader would not start; it also left the menu hidden.

press_80ms.rig_result: ok true, fidelity wire-sent, usb-hid:bridge, ack buttons 4096 (0x1000)
press_80ms.plain: A Steam-button press arrived: key code 316 (BTN_MODE) value 1, then released value 0, 80 ms later (244.019 to 244.099). Nothing else arrived. The Steam main menu did NOT open (MainMenu page stayed hidden, checked about 3 s after).

press_150ms.plain: Code 316 value 1 then value 0, 150 ms apart (262.821 to 262.971). Nothing else. The main menu did NOT open.

press_400ms.plain: Code 316 value 1 then value 0, 400 ms apart (280.658 to 281.058). Nothing else. The main menu did NOT open.

chord_steam_plus_a.plain: Code 316 down at 296.718; code 304 (BTN_SOUTH, the A button) down at 296.986 (268 ms later); A up at 297.125 (139 ms held); Steam button up at 297.286. Total 568 ms with A inside the Steam hold. Quick Access DID open (QuickAccess page visible, plugin panel mounted, screenshot shows the panel).

expected: Findings only: what the Deck receives when the rig presses the Steam button.
verdict: PASS (findings recorded) - the Deck's input system receives a clean press and release of the Steam button (code 316) at 80, 150 and 400 ms, with nothing extra, but Steam's main menu does not open for a bare press at any of the three lengths. The same button inside the chord (held 568 ms with A) does open Quick Access.

UNCLEAR - why a bare press does nothing: the Deck sees the events, so the board and the hold time are not the cause. What the runbook did not test: how Steam treats a Steam-button press that is not followed by anything (it may need the press to arrive while the Steam page has input focus, or a different hold).
cleanup: Reader and its output files removed from the Deck (/tmp has no p89 files left; no p89 service units left). Raw files copied to the scratch folder as m3-ev_1.txt to m3-ev_4.txt. Quick Access left open, the plugin panel on screen.
